Flat 2D cartoon historical illustration. Round-headed people with age-appropriate adult and child proportions where specified, dot eyes, expressive eyebrows, simple rounded hands, clean medium-weight dark-brown outlines (#2B1D14), flat earthy ochre, olive, brick, slate and parchment colours with soft cel shading. Match the season drawing style, never the style reference's setting. Full-bleed 16:9, 2K, one clear focal point.
Historical scope: Queen Anne's Revenge, early 1718; illustrative working deck.
Early 1718, aboard a reconstruction of Queen Anne's Revenge off the southeastern coast of North America, before her June grounding. Low timber working decks, hemp rope, wooden blocks, plain canvas sails, wooden barrels and plain clothing: linen shirts, waistcoats, breeches, caps and soft felt hats. No claim to an archaeologically certain deck plan. The same modest working space and adult crew recur. Modern archaeological explanations use neutral parchment; the clearly labelled Roberts comparison belongs to another crew in 1719–1722.
Location/object design: Timber bulwark left with sea beyond, one mast base rear-left, a neatly secured rope coil at left, clear level deck on right. No wheel, flags, guns firing or exact unsupported vessel silhouette. Adult sailor A: brown waistcoat, cream shirt, slate breeches, plain brown cap.
reaction: Empty established deck, calm slate sea, rope coil left.
